videos.script: Every server can do a fixed number of things at once. Threads, connections to the database, memory. The number is usually set by a default nobody chose. {{fixed}} This lesson is about what happens when something uses all of them. {{all}} On your machine, Quitanda's shop has eight threads. One dependency, the stock service, becomes slow. Within seconds, the catalogue, which never calls the stock service, stops answering too. {{slow}} You will fix that with a bulkhead, named after the walls that divide a ship's hull, so that one flooded compartment does not sink it. {{bulkhead}} Then a client that asks far too often, and a limit that tells it so, with the status code made for that. {{limit}} And a queue in front of the orders, which absorbs a sudden rush, until you look at how long the last order waited. {{queue}} All three are the same idea: a system that says no early, to some of the work, keeps doing the rest.
